summary: The study investigates the etching effect of NbCl5 on Nb2O5 thin films during atomic layer deposition (ALD). It demonstrates that NbCl5 etches Nb2O5, forming volatile NbOCl3, which is removed from the surface. The process is studied in-situ using quadrupole mass spectrometry (QMS) and quartz crystal microbalance (QCM). The results suggest that Nb2O5 can be deposited from in-situ-generated NbOCl3, which is formed from NbCl5 and D2O.
evidence: Nb2O5 is deposited from Nb(OEt)5 and water in the same reactor. NbCl5 is found to etch the Nb2O5 film producing volatile NbOCl3. The temperature in our experiments was 250 8C. The QCM results show that the mass decreases during the NbCl5 pulses as soon as the process stabilizes. The QMS results show that the signal m/z ¼ 216 is observed during the NbCl5 pulses. This m/z corresponds to the molecular peak of NbOCl3.
